run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T22:40:24Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: Alert RequestErrorRate (warning) fired for otel-demo/frontend-proxy at 2026-11-16T22:40:24Z with a reported current value of 0.0111. The only request-error signal this Prometheus holds for frontend-proxy is the trace-derived series traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}; there are no http_server_* or rpc_* series in the window. Observed: frontend-proxy's error status is not a steady state - the ingress error-rate series is 0 through 22:40:00, 0.0111 at 22:41:00 and 22:43:00, spikes to 1.0333 at 22:45:00, and is back to ~0 by 22:46:00, with an earlier burst of 0.1266 at 22:23:24 and 0.1153 at 22:25:24. Its logs show two distinct failure shapes: twenty 504 UT response_timeout responses (15 000-15 002 ms) on GET /api/data between 22:20:37 and 22:21:00, then sporadic 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} responses from 22:21:26 to 22:41:11 and again at 22:44:11, 22:45:17, 22:47:30 and 22:49:59. A full trace at 22:20:46 shows the 504 path end to end: load-generator GET -> frontend-proxy ingress 15.0 s with 504 -> frontend GET /api/data 27.97 s -> grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 27.97 s -> ad oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 22.50 s -> ad resolve spans of 5.10 s and 3.00 s containing flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean spans with error=true and rpc.grpc.status_code=4. The 503 shape is the frontend (the proxy's upstream) terminating the connection: those traces contain frontend-proxy ingress/egress and load-generator spans only, with no frontend span. The frontend's own error spans are confined to 22:43-22:45 and are cart/checkout calls (AddItem 0.578/s, GetCart 0.256/s, PlaceOrder 0.200/s), overlapping a Deployment cart rollout restart (new ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d annotated kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T22:42:54Z, old pod killed 22:42:57, new cart container started 22:42:56 but logged "Now listening on" only at 22:43:22). ConfigMap flagd-config currently has the fault-injection flag cartFailure=on ("Fail cart service") with all other fault flags off, but counter-evidence (cart served requests and the proxy logged 200 for /api/cart at 22:45-22:49 while the flag reads on) keeps it a hypothesis. Ad and flagd pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts, and no networkpolicies or resourcequotas exist in otel-demo. Leading hypotheses, none established as the single origin: (1) ad-service flag resolution against flagd timing out (gRPC 4) drove the 22:20 /api/data timeouts past the proxy's 15 s limit; (2) the frontend intermittently terminates upstream connections for a reason not visible here because its container logs are empty; (3) the 22:43-22:45 burst was caused by the cart restart gap. Separately, fraud-detection's container was OOMKilled (exit 137) at 22:48:24 and restarted - a change during the window for its own reason, not tied to the alert path. Because two different failure origins remain and no single object is established, root_cause is null and the conclusion is partial.

claims.text: In this Prometheus the frontend-proxy request metrics are trace-derived only: traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket, with series service_name="frontend-proxy", span_name="ingress" (SPAN_KIND_SERVER) and span_name="router frontend egress" (SPAN_KIND_CLIENT), each in status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET; no other metric family carries the label service_name="frontend-proxy" in 21:40:24-23:01:36.

Whole-window increase (4 872 s range) for frontend-proxy: span_name "ingress" STATUS_CODE_ERROR 143.2 versus 22 299.9 STATUS_CODE_UNSET, and span_name "router frontend egress" STATUS_CODE_ERROR 94.5 versus 22 352.9 STATUS_CODE_UNSET.

frontend-proxy container logs for 22:15:00-22:45:00 contain twenty "504 UT response_timeout" responses on GET /api/data between 22:20:37 and 22:21:00 (durations 15 000, 15 001 and 15 002 ms), then "503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}" responses at 22:21:26, 22:22:22 (x2), 22:22:38, 22:23:54 (x2), 22:25:58, 22:27:01, 22:28:14, 22:29:28 (x2), 22:31:19, 22:31:31, 22:39:11 and 22:41:11.

More 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} lines occur at 22:44:11 (three lines, on GET /api/products/66VCHSJNUP, /LS4PSXUNUM and /9SIQT8TOJO), 22:45:17, 22:47:30 and 22:49:59 in the frontend-proxy log.

Trace 77b4faa8908c1a39f12f412fe27b7327 (start 22:20:46) shows: load-generator user_get_ads 15.985 s with child GET error=true http.status_code 504; frontend-proxy ingress 15.001 s error=true http.status_code 504; frontend-proxy "router frontend egress" 15.001 s error="true" http.status_code "0"; frontend "GET" 14.906 s http.status_code 200; frontend "GET /api/data" 27.971 s http.status_code 200; frontend "grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds" 27.970 s; ad "oteldemo.AdService/GetAds" 22.500 s; ad "resolve" spans of 5.101 s and 3.001 s, each containing ad "flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean" spans with error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR and rpc.grpc.status_code=4.

Sampled 503 traces at 22:25:58-22:28:15 contain only frontend-proxy ingress (503, error=true), frontend-proxy "router frontend egress" (error="true", http.status_code "0") and load-generator spans (error=true, http.status_code 503) - no frontend service span is present in those traces.

The frontend service's own ERROR spans occur only in the 22:43:00-22:45:00 interval: at the 22:45:00 point grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 0.578/s, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 0.256/s, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 0.200/s, GET 0.256/s, POST 0.778/s, POST /api/cart 0.578/s, POST /api/checkout 0.200/s, executing api route (pages) /api/cart 0.833/s and tcp.connect 0.078/s, while every sampled 5-minute point from 22:25:24 to 22:55:24 outside that interval is 0.

Deployment cart was restarted at 22:42:54: event Deployment/cart ScalingReplicaSet "Scaled up replica set cart-84889c965d from 0 to 1" at 22:42:54 and "Scaled down replica set cart-755465879b from 1 to 0" at 22:42:57, with ReplicaSet cart-755465879b SuccessfulDelete of pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4 (Pod event Killing "Stopping container cart") at 22:42:57; ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d carries pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T22:42:54Z and an otherwise identical pod template (same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart, same env, resources cpu 45m/memory 165Mi, same busybox wait-for-valkey-cart init container) as revision 1.

The replacement cart container started at 22:42:56 but its log shows "Successfully connected to Redis" only at 22:43:10 and "Now listening on: {address}" / "Application started" at 22:43:22, so the cart endpoint was not serving for roughly the first 25 s of the new pod's life; the pod is now Running and Ready with restartCount 0.

Cart served traffic after the restart: cart log lines "AddItemAsync called ..." / "GetCartAsync called ..." at 22:45:24, 22:46:03 and 22:52:33, and in 22:50:00-23:00:00 cart span rates HGET 4.60/s, HMSET 2.18/s, POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 1.61/s and POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 2.91/s all with status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET, with the only cart ERROR series (flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream) reading 0.

ConfigMap flagd-config in otel-demo defines the fault-injection flags and currently has cartFailure defaultVariant "on" ("Fail cart service"), while adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure are all "off".

A trace in 22:24:00-22:29:00 shows ad's client span flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream starting 22:28:18 lasting 600.002 s with error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR and rpc.grpc.status_code=4, whose child is service "flagd" (service_version v0.12.8) with the same 600 s duration, error=true and error detail otel.status_description="stream closed due to server-side timeout".

All otel-demo pods are Running and Ready; restartCount is 0 for every container except fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh, whose container lastState is terminated reason OOMKilled exitCode 137 finishedAt 2026-11-16T22:48:24Z with restartCount 1 and current state running startedAt 2026-11-16T22:48:25Z.
Whole-window ERROR-span increase by service: frontend 385.2, frontend-proxy 237.7, recommendation 4.07, ad 2.04, fraud-detection 2.04, and exactly 0 for accounting, cart, checkout and payment.
There are no networkpolicies and no resourcequotas in the otel-demo namespace (both queries returned zero objects).

No baseline exists in this data: a 24-hour range query of the frontend-proxy ingress error rate returned its earliest sample at 22:26:36 (three points only), and all otel-demo pod startTime values are 22:11:44-22:11:57, so the workload and its span metrics began around 22:11-22:16 and no pre-incident error baseline is available.

The span duration histogram is unusable for latency here: every traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket series for service_name="ad", span_name="resolve" (all le values from 2.0 to +Inf) reads exactly 0 across 22:15:00-23:01:36.

The 504 timeouts that started the deviation at 22:20:37 were produced by ad-service feature-flag resolution against flagd: ad's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds took 22.5 s with ad resolve spans of 3-5 s containing flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean spans ending rpc.grpc.status_code=4, which raised frontend GET /api/data to 27.97 s and exceeded frontend-proxy's 15 s response timeout ("504 UT response_timeout"). The object this would implicate is Deployment flagd in otel-demo, supported by the flagd-side span error "stream closed due to server-side timeout"; it is not established because flagd's container produced no readable log lines and no flagd-side metric is available.

The sporadic 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} responses (22:21:26-22:41:11, the errors dominating the period before the alert's 22:40:24 start) are the frontend closing the upstream connection: the proxy's egress span reports error with http.status_code 0 after 0.49-0.89 s and the corresponding 503 traces carry no frontend span at all. Why the frontend terminates these connections is unknown - one possibility is saturation caused by the long-hanging /api/data requests - because the frontend container yielded no readable log lines and no CPU-throttling metric exists here.

The 22:43-22:45 error burst (frontend-proxy 1.0333/s at 22:45:00, frontend cart/checkout client-span errors, 503s at 22:44:11-22:45:17) was caused by the cart Deployment restart at 22:42:54 removing the only cart pod at 22:42:57 while the replacement did not begin listening until 22:43:22, so frontend calls to CartService/GetCart, CartService/AddItem and CheckoutService/PlaceOrder failed in exactly that interval. The restart's trigger is not observable (change_history integration not available).

The fault-injection setting cartFailure="on" ("Fail cart service") in ConfigMap flagd-config may be the injected fault behind the observed cart-call failures; it is kept only as a hypothesis because the cart errors are limited to the cart restart interval and the flag's state during the incident is unknown (the ConfigMap was read at 23:02, after the covered window).

The alert's reported value 0.0111 equals the single-error rate 1/90 s that this spanmetric series yields (0.0111 = 1/90), so RequestErrorRate appears to fire on a near-zero threshold when the first error appears in its evaluation window; the alert expression cannot be confirmed because no alerting or recording rules are loaded in this Prometheus.

The enabled cartFailure flag does not explain a continuous cart failure: cart served AddItem/GetCart at 22:45:24, 22:46:03 and 22:52:33, its Redis-span and AddItem/GetCart span rates are normal with STATUS_CODE_UNSET and no cart ERROR series above 0 in 22:50-23:00, and frontend-proxy logged POST /api/cart and GET /api/cart as 200 at 22:49:55-22:49:59 while the ConfigMap reads cartFailure="on".

No pod of the implicated services crashed or restarted: ad-554b849958-fbw9s (container started 22:11:48, restartCount 0), flagd-77f6d5b95d-64j8j (both containers started 22:13:41, restartCount 0), frontend-675fd7b5c5-64mj8 (22:11:46, restartCount 0), frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-v4lvt (22:11:49, restartCount 0) and cart-84889c965d-tkxdz (22:42:56, restartCount 0) are all Running and Ready.

Most backend services recorded no errors of their own in the window: accounting, cart, checkout and payment each have an ERROR-span increase of exactly 0, and recommendation (4.07), ad (2.04) and fraud-detection (2.04) only small counts, so this is not a namespace-wide failure and cart's own spans never carried an error status.

frontend-proxy itself is not the origin of the errors: its pod has restartCount 0, its ingress spans mirror upstream behaviour (egress "router frontend egress" error with http.status_code 0 on the same trace), and the logged failure mode is upstream connection termination/reset from the frontend, not a proxy-generated fault.

The fraud-detection OOMKill (exit 137 at 22:48:24) is not this alert's cause: it happened after the alert started at 22:40:24, fraud-detection recorded only 2.04 error spans over the whole window, and the observed failure path runs through frontend/ad/cart rather than fraud-detection.
Network policy or namespace quota misconfiguration is not a factor: no networkpolicies and no resourcequotas exist in otel-demo.

Retrieve the RequestErrorRate rule definition (expression, threshold, evaluation window) from the alerting source that produced the Alertmanager notification, since this Prometheus returned no loaded alerting or recording rules, to confirm whether the alert is a >0 tripwire over the spanmetrics error series.

Check container CPU throttling and memory pressure for ad (cpu limit 50m), frontend (100m) and frontend-proxy (30m) - cAdvisor-style metrics are absent from this target - to test whether the frontend resets and ad slowness reflect CPU starvation, and review flagd's stream deadline configuration for ad's 600 s flag event stream.

Find out what issued the cart Deployment rollout restart recorded as kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T22:42:54Z (change history is not integrated here) and whether the flagd-config cartFailure flag was toggled around that time, then re-test cart behaviour with the flag on to see whether the enabled fault explains the 22:43-22:45 cart errors.

The frontend-proxy span metrics have no samples before about 22:16-22:26 and the whole otel-demo namespace started at 22:11, so there is no pre-incident baseline and no latency or error trend can be established.
The value and content of ConfigMap flagd-config during the incident window are unknown; the read reflects the cluster state at 23:02.

Truncated or incomplete views limit some observations: c07a3c97-bd06-4f20-a116-f53b1e5302a8-t0:7a4fcbfe-13a3-4204-af4f-c4789e1bcced shows only 50 of 233 sampled error rows, e2b27737-4bfa-4a24-ba9c-74715616e8d9-t0:3a5de168-89dd-4ad7-aa1c-4711568a36d4 stopped at the 4 MiB read limit (through 22:41:14) and ff83f563-e56a-4d39-8abf-ea7311f24b15-t1:c0aceb93-59b2-40ec-8491-cbaa91c34ecf plus f0909afd-7023-4db1-b63d-454a406c7da2-t0:a9c04464-8420-489a-bc6a-ea549e45762e are flagged incomplete, so error and log counts should be read as samples, not totals.

No baseline exists in this data: a 24-hour range query of the frontend-proxy ingress error rate returned its earliest sample at 22:26:36 (three points only), and all otel-demo pod startTime values are 22:11:44-22:11:57, so the workload and its span metrics began around 22:11-22:16 and no pre-incident error baseline is available.

The span duration histogram is unusable for latency here: every traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket series for service_name="ad", span_name="resolve" (all le values from 2.0 to +Inf) reads exactly 0 across 22:15:00-23:01:36.

hypothesis.text: The 504 timeouts that started the deviation at 22:20:37 were produced by ad-service feature-flag resolution against flagd: ad's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds took 22.5 s with ad resolve spans of 3-5 s containing flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean spans ending rpc.grpc.status_code=4, which raised frontend GET /api/data to 27.97 s and exceeded frontend-proxy's 15 s response timeout ("504 UT response_timeout"). The object this would implicate is Deployment flagd in otel-demo, supported by the flagd-side span error "stream closed due to server-side timeout"; it is not established because flagd's container produced no readable log lines and no flagd-side metric is available.

The sporadic 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} responses (22:21:26-22:41:11, the errors dominating the period before the alert's 22:40:24 start) are the frontend closing the upstream connection: the proxy's egress span reports error with http.status_code 0 after 0.49-0.89 s and the corresponding 503 traces carry no frontend span at all. Why the frontend terminates these connections is unknown - one possibility is saturation caused by the long-hanging /api/data requests - because the frontend container yielded no readable log lines and no CPU-throttling metric exists here.

The 22:43-22:45 error burst (frontend-proxy 1.0333/s at 22:45:00, frontend cart/checkout client-span errors, 503s at 22:44:11-22:45:17) was caused by the cart Deployment restart at 22:42:54 removing the only cart pod at 22:42:57 while the replacement did not begin listening until 22:43:22, so frontend calls to CartService/GetCart, CartService/AddItem and CheckoutService/PlaceOrder failed in exactly that interval. The restart's trigger is not observable (change_history integration not available).

The fault-injection setting cartFailure="on" ("Fail cart service") in ConfigMap flagd-config may be the injected fault behind the observed cart-call failures; it is kept only as a hypothesis because the cart errors are limited to the cart restart interval and the flag's state during the incident is unknown (the ConfigMap was read at 23:02, after the covered window).

The alert's reported value 0.0111 equals the single-error rate 1/90 s that this spanmetric series yields (0.0111 = 1/90), so RequestErrorRate appears to fire on a near-zero threshold when the first error appears in its evaluation window; the alert expression cannot be confirmed because no alerting or recording rules are loaded in this Prometheus.

recommendation.text: Retrieve the RequestErrorRate rule definition (expression, threshold, evaluation window) from the alerting source that produced the Alertmanager notification, since this Prometheus returned no loaded alerting or recording rules, to confirm whether the alert is a >0 tripwire over the spanmetrics error series.

Check container CPU throttling and memory pressure for ad (cpu limit 50m), frontend (100m) and frontend-proxy (30m) - cAdvisor-style metrics are absent from this target - to test whether the frontend resets and ad slowness reflect CPU starvation, and review flagd's stream deadline configuration for ad's 600 s flag event stream.

Find out what issued the cart Deployment rollout restart recorded as kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T22:42:54Z (change history is not integrated here) and whether the flagd-config cartFailure flag was toggled around that time, then re-test cart behaviour with the flag on to see whether the enabled fault explains the 22:43-22:45 cart errors.

counter_evidence.text: The enabled cartFailure flag does not explain a continuous cart failure: cart served AddItem/GetCart at 22:45:24, 22:46:03 and 22:52:33, its Redis-span and AddItem/GetCart span rates are normal with STATUS_CODE_UNSET and no cart ERROR series above 0 in 22:50-23:00, and frontend-proxy logged POST /api/cart and GET /api/cart as 200 at 22:49:55-22:49:59 while the ConfigMap reads cartFailure="on".

No pod of the implicated services crashed or restarted: ad-554b849958-fbw9s (container started 22:11:48, restartCount 0), flagd-77f6d5b95d-64j8j (both containers started 22:13:41, restartCount 0), frontend-675fd7b5c5-64mj8 (22:11:46, restartCount 0), frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-v4lvt (22:11:49, restartCount 0) and cart-84889c965d-tkxdz (22:42:56, restartCount 0) are all Running and Ready.

Most backend services recorded no errors of their own in the window: accounting, cart, checkout and payment each have an ERROR-span increase of exactly 0, and recommendation (4.07), ad (2.04) and fraud-detection (2.04) only small counts, so this is not a namespace-wide failure and cart's own spans never carried an error status.

rejected_hypothesis.text: frontend-proxy itself is not the origin of the errors: its pod has restartCount 0, its ingress spans mirror upstream behaviour (egress "router frontend egress" error with http.status_code 0 on the same trace), and the logged failure mode is upstream connection termination/reset from the frontend, not a proxy-generated fault.

The fraud-detection OOMKill (exit 137 at 22:48:24) is not this alert's cause: it happened after the alert started at 22:40:24, fraud-detection recorded only 2.04 error spans over the whole window, and the observed failure path runs through frontend/ad/cart rather than fraud-detection.
Network policy or namespace quota misconfiguration is not a factor: no networkpolicies and no resourcequotas exist in otel-demo.
